About the Role
We’re looking for a Facebook Ads Specialist to take ownership of Facebook advertising campaigns from strategy and setup through ongoing optimization. You’ll manage campaign performance, audiences, budgets, testing, and reporting while working closely with the marketing team to improve results.
What You’ll Own
Campaign Planning & Strategy

• Design and build Facebook ad campaigns from the ground up.

• Align targeting, creative direction, and budget allocation with business objectives.

Ad Execution & Management

• Set up, launch, and actively manage Facebook campaigns.

• Monitor delivery, pacing, and performance on an ongoing basis.

Audience Development

• Research, build, and refine audience segments.

• Use custom audiences, lookalikes, and interest-based targeting to improve reach and relevance.

Performance Analysis & Reporting

• Track key metrics across active campaigns.

• Analyze campaign data and identify trends.

• Turn findings into clear recommendations for improving performance.

Creative Collaboration

• Ensure assets are optimized for their placement and campaign objective.

Budget Management

Testing & Optimization

• Run structured A/B tests across audiences, creatives, and landing page combinations.

• Apply learnings systematically across campaigns.

Required Experience & Skills

• Proven hands-on experience planning and running Facebook ad campaigns, ideally in a marketing agency or similarly fast-moving environment.

• Strong command of Meta Ads Manager, including campaign structure, pixel setup, conversion tracking, and attribution settings.

• Experience managing ad budgets and being accountable for performance results.

• Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret campaign data and identify trends.

• Experience with A/B testing and a disciplined approach to applying campaign learnings.

• Confident communication skills with the ability to present performance updates and recommendations clearly.

What Makes You a Strong Fit

• You take ownership of campaign outcomes from launch through optimization.

• You’re comfortable working independently in a remote environment.

• You communicate proactively and flag issues early.

• You make decisions based on data rather than assumptions or habits.

• You’re detail-oriented while keeping the broader campaign strategy in focus.

What Success Looks Like

• Campaigns are launched with clear targeting, creative direction, and budget strategy.

• Campaign performance is consistently monitored and optimized.

• Ad spend is managed responsibly against performance targets.

• A/B testing generates actionable insights that improve campaign results.

• The marketing team receives clear, useful performance updates and recommendations.

Typical Day
Your day centers on the Focusmediahouse ad accounts. You’ll start by reviewing overnight performance across live campaigns and identifying opportunities for budget adjustments, creative changes, or targeting improvements.
You may then prepare performance reports, brief a designer on a new creative concept, or build the structure for an upcoming campaign. Testing is an ongoing part of the role, including reviewing active experiments, deciding what to scale or cut, and setting up the next round.
Most collaboration happens asynchronously, so strong written communication and clear documentation are important.

Growcer builds the infrastructure for food sovereignty. We provide communities, Indigenous nations, schools, hospitals, and institutions across North America with the tools, training, and support to grow food locally, 365 days a year. We don't just sell container farms; we help communities go from dependence to self-reliance, one harvest at a time.
Growcer is looking for a driven individual with a self-starter attitude as the company enters the next phase of rapid growth and scales across North America. Effective Growcer employees are tenacious, enjoy working in a fast-paced environment, and are comfortable working on big-picture challenges with lots of autonomy.
If you want your work to be visible, your impact to be direct, and your mission to be one you'd be proud to explain at a dinner party, you'll feel right at home.

As a Horticulture Support Manager, you are a vital piece to the Growcer organization leading the hands-on installation and on-going technical support for new and current farms. You'll help train customers in how to best run their farms and support them in trouble shooting, work to create training and other internal materials as well as contribute with ideas to improve the overall quality of the farms.

Experience in a greenhouse or other Controlled Environment Agriculture (CEA) setting is an asset, but most of the horticulture side can be learned on the job by following established SOPs. title: Senior Software Engineer - Data Search (remote, Europe)
description: Hey, I'm Adrian . I’m hiring a Senior Software Engineer to join the Data Search team at Modash. Modash helps brands find, understand, and work with creators across Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube. More than 2,700 companies-including Stanley 1913, Sennheiser, and NordVPN-use us to manage and scale their creator partnerships. Behind that product is a fascinating search problem: helping customers find the right people across 400M+ creator profiles and billions of media files. We’re combining large-scale data processing, traditional retrieval, vector search, multimodal embeddings, and LLMs to make that possible. That’s where you come in. Why we're hiring Search at Modash isn't an internal platform or a support function. It is one of the core products customers use to discover creators. The scale is large, the data is messy, and the search intent is often complex. A customer might be looking for creators in a specific niche, people whose content conveys a certain visual style, or accounts that resemble a group they already know. Solving that well requires more than adding another filter or calling an LLM API. We need a senior engineer who can work across the full retrieval system-from data and indexing pipelines to embeddings, ranking, relevance, and low-latency serving-and take ambiguous product problems all the way to production. You’ll join the specialised Data Search team and work closely with Data Core, Data Insights, product teams, customers, and company leadership. You’ll have real autonomy, but you won’t work in isolation. If you want a feel for how we think about building software, check our Engineering Blog . What you'll actually own 1. title: Applied Scientist / Machine Learning Engineer
description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Wayve’s engineering teams are building the AI, robotics, simulation, data, and systems foundations needed to deploy a generalisable AI Driver safely and at scale.

The Enrichment and Curation team transforms fleet-scale driving data into high-quality training datasets, enrichments, and evaluation benchmarks for Wayve’s end-to-end AI Driver and foundation models.

- Build scalable methods to discover rare, high-value, and safety-critical scenarios in fleet data.

- Data engines and retrieval systems using Python, SQL, Spark, embeddings, and multimodal models.

- Training-data strategy for embodied vision-language and driving models.

- Automated enrichment, active learning, and model-assisted labelling.

- Evaluation datasets that connect data decisions to real-world driving outcomes.

title: Senior Engineer, FDE (Agentic & Eco-System)

description:
Job Overview
We’re looking for a Cloud & Infrastructure Engineer to build, secure, and maintain scalable platform infrastructure and delivery pipelines. The ideal candidate combines hands-on experience with managed PaaS platforms and core AWS services (RDS, S3, Lambda) with strong capabilities in Infrastructure as Code, automated CI/CD, and transactional email deliverability. This role will collaborate closely with project leads and software engineers, establish comprehensive observability and security controls, and deliver reliable, automated, and well-documented cloud environments.
Core Tasks
1. Cloud architecture and platform

• Assess the current infrastructure - what is running, how it is configured, what is manual, and where the risk sits - and produce a written assessment with prioritized findings.

• Define and implement the target infrastructure across PaaS platform, e.g., Heroku, Render, Elastic Beanstalk, App Runner and supporting AWS services, with environment separation for dev / staging / production.

• Define infrastructure as code so environments are reproducible rather than hand-configured. Terraform / CloudFormation / CDK / Pulumi, as agreed.

• Implement IAM roles and least-privilege access, secrets management, and network configuration (VPC, security groups, TLS).

2. Data and storage layer

• RDS: provision and tune the database - instance sizing, parameter groups, connection pooling, read replicas if warranted - and configure automated backups, point-in-time recovery, and encryption at rest.

• Run and document a restore test. A backup that has never been restored is not a backup.

• S3: configure buckets for uploads / assets / exports / logs with correct access policies, lifecycle rules, versioning, and encryption. No public buckets that should not be public.

• Set up CDN delivery for static and user-uploaded assets where appropriate.

3.Serverless and background processing

• Review the stack against HIPAA / PCI / SOC 2 / other requirements where applicable, and document what is in place and what is not.

title: Recruiting Operations Coordinator
description:
OUR VISION

Health systems still run critical operations like staffing, labor planning, and capacity on spreadsheets, phone calls, and guesswork.

Vitalize is building the AI operating system for how health systems manage labor and capacity. The impact is real: we save hospitals millions in unnecessary labor spend, give clinical leaders back 10-20 hours every week, and are often the reason staff and leaders stay.

We’re trusted by leading health systems across the country and have raised more than $31M from top healthcare and technology investors, including our own customers.

OUR VALUES

We hire and grow everyone against the same four values. Each one comes from a real Vitalize story-interview with us to hear them!

- 🚗 Push the Car. Step in regardless of role. We help wherever we're needed, own problems end to end, and don't stay in our lane. People can count on us.

- 🏥 Premier 1K. We show up for our customers, always. Nearly everyone visits a customer site in their first month, and customer feedback informs everything we do.

- 🗣️ Run Towards the Ugly. Name the ugliest truth first, then propose the fix. Candor over comfort-we call out what's broken, and never get complacent. This shapes our craft.

- 💡 Think Bigger Fridays. See the gap, fill it-no permission required. Every decision is an experiment: we run it, let the results decide, and drive real impact from day one.

ABOUT VITALIZE'S TALENT TEAM

The Talent Team will determine how quickly Vitalize scales and how much impact we can have on healthcare. Every great hire helps us deploy faster, build better products, serve more hospitals, and ultimately improve the way care is delivered.

We're building what we believe will become one of the best talent teams in the world. We don't believe great recruiting starts with a job description; it starts with deeply understanding our customers, the problems we're solving, and the teams we're building. Our recruiters sit in on customer calls, travel to customer sites, partner closely with hiring teams, and immerse themselves in the business so they can recruit with credibility. As one of our founding recruiters, you'll help build our talent function from the ground up and shape how Vitalize hires for years to come.

THE ROLE

This isn't a traditional recruiting coordinator role. You'll be the operational backbone of our Talent team as we scale and build-the person constantly looking for better ways to hire. When you see friction, you fix it. When you notice repetitive work, you automate it. When a process doesn't scale, you build one that does. You find satisfaction in making complex things feel effortless.

You'll become our in-house Ashby expert, pushing the platform beyond the basics by building automations, creating thoughtful interview kits, improving workflows, leveraging AI, and ensuring every part of our hiring process gets a little better every week. You're the type of person who loves tinkering with systems and is always asking, "There has to be a better way to do this."

You'll also own some of the most important moments in a candidate's and employee's journey. Whether it's creating a seamless interview experience or ensuring every new hire has an incredible first day, you sweat the small details because you know they're what people remember.

Finally, we believe sourcing is one of the highest-leverage skills in recruiting, and we want everyone on our Talent team to learn it. We'll teach you how to identify exceptional talent, build talent maps, develop thoughtful outreach strategies, and proactively engage candidates long before they're looking for their next opportunity. Over time, you'll become one of our secret weapons-not because you manage the process, but because you consistently help us find incredible people.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Own interview operations across the company, ensuring every interview is thoughtfully coordinated and every candidate has an exceptional experience

title: Marketing Operations & AI Specialist (Full Time, Remote)
description:
About Frontier

Frontier is a subsidiary of Fresh Prints . Fresh Prints is a New York-based, fast-growing, fully remote, 150-person company with most of our team based in India and the Philippines. A few years ago, Fresh Prints began helping other fast-growing companies build their teams. We got so good at it that we spun out a new company to focus exclusively on that - and called it Frontier .

We help companies grow cross-functional teams abroad. We hire the smartest people and place them into great companies. If you're interested in a Frontier role and you apply and are accepted, we'll screen you through assessments and interviews and aim to connect you with the right opportunity.

About the client

Balto is building the AI Workforce for contact centers, and needs a Marketing Operations and AI Specialist who keeps the marketing engine clean, measurable, and running. You'll own the data, the attribution, and the day-to-day operations that keep the BDR team productive. This role is for someone who sees a tedious, manual process and immediately starts building a way to never do it by hand again. You'll use AI to build tools and workflows that take the busywork off everyone's plate. You understand why the work matters, not just how to do it, and you'd rather bring a solution than wait for instructions.

What You'll Own

Data Quality

• Clean up and maintain contact, account, and lead data across HubSpot and Salesforce

• Find the root cause of bad data, fix it, and put a process in place so it doesn't come back

• Build AI-powered workflows that handle enrichment, deduplication, and cleanup so no one does it by hand

Marketing and Campaign Attribution

• Own marketing and campaign attribution from first touch to closed-won

• Make sure every campaign is tracked correctly so the company knows what's actually driving pipeline

• Build reports that answer real questions and help the team decide where to spend time and money

List Building

• Build and enrich target lists in Clay and TitanX based on Balto's ICP and target accounts

• Keep lists accurate, deduplicated, and ready to use

Process and Tool Building

• Spot manual, repetitive work and replace it with automations, AI agents, or simple tools

• Solve problems on your own, and come to the table with a recommendation, not just the problem

• Document processes, fields, and changes, and tell the right people when something changes and why it matters

BDR Operations

• Build reports that show each BDR's activity: calls, emails, and who's getting contacted

• Decide which lists should be sequenced, and load contacts into Outreach sequences for the BDRs

• Monitor BDR task loads and sequence capacity to make sure workloads are realistic and lists are being worked effectively.

• Surface gaps early, whether that's a rep falling behind on assigned tasks, a list running dry, or a sequence underperforming.

What You Bring to the Table

You don't need to have done every single one of these. But the more that sound like you, the better:

• 3+ years in marketing operations, sales operations, or revenue operations at a B2B company

• Extremely detail-oriented. You notice the duplicate record, the broken field mapping, and the campaign that isn't tracking before anyone else does

• You understand the business. You know why a report matters, who uses it, and what decision it drives

• You think for yourself. Give you a problem and you'll investigate it, ask the right questions, and come back with a recommended solution.

• You communicate clearly when things change: new processes, new fields, new rules, and what people need to do differently

• Hands-on experience with attribution models and campaign tracking

• Comfortable working with large datasets in spreadsheets, including formulas, lookups, filtering, and data cleanup.

• Experience supporting BDR or SDR teams with reporting, list building, or sequencing

Tools You'll Work With

• Claude

• HubSpot

• Salesforce

• Clay

• Outreach

title: Staff GTM Systems Engineer
description:
ABOUT CODERABBIT

CodeRabbit is the leading AI code review platform, trusted by more than 17,000 customers and 150,000 open-source projects, conducting over 2 million code reviews each week. We build the symbiotic partnership between developers and AI that makes shipping fast software safe again, reviewing every pull request, IDE change, and CLI commit so teams can move quickly without breaking things.

 

We are a fast-moving, well-funded company, fresh off a $143M Series C at a $1.5B valuation - building Agentic Change Management, the control layer for software changes created by humans and agents. As AI writes more of the world's code, the bottleneck moves from implementation to judgment and helping human judgment scale is exactly the problem we exist to solve.

THE OPPORTUNITY

At CodeRabbit, our agents already write, review, and ship our Salesforce and internal tooling code. A Linear label or Slack emoji starts a pipeline: an agent plans the change, a human approves, the agent builds and tests it in a sandbox and opens a pull request, a second model reviews it, and guard hooks stop anything that could hurt production. This is our GTM Systems harness. We're looking for a Staff GTM Systems Engineer to own it and to architect the systems it builds: the pipeline generation, quote-to-cash, provisioning, and billing integrations behind a company growing from PLG into enterprise sales, and the internal tools our GTM teams run on. You'll be the senior technical voice in Business Systems, setting the patterns that engineers, analysts and agents all follow.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

- Own and evolve the agentic engineering harness: the Agent Build pipeline, guard hooks, worktree tooling, CI, model routing and the permission tiers that keep agents safe around production.

- Design and build internal tools and agents as full-stack applications (TypeScript, Next.js, Postgres, MCP servers) where off-the-shelf software falls short.

- Build in Salesforce at a deep level: Apex service and selector patterns, triggers, LWC, Platform Events, permission sets and the metadata deployment model.

- Set the engineering standards for Business Systems: architecture reviews, code review, testing, release and production runbooks, and how agent-written work gets reviewed and shipped.

- Give the analysts and engineers on the team the platform to build their own agents, such as the Sales OS Agent and Data Quality Agent.

- Partner with Finance, GTM, Deal Desk, and the Data teams to turn ambiguous business needs into systems that hold up at the next stage of scale.

- Raise the technical bar across the team through pairing, reviews and design docs, and reduce our dependence on outside consultants over time.

QUALIFICATIONS

- Deep, hands-on Salesforce engineering: Apex, LWC, data modeling, sharing and security, and source-driven deployment with the Salesforce CLI.

- Strong full-stack software engineering beyond Salesforce, with production web apps, APIs and databases you have built and run.

- Real experience building with agentic coding tools such as Claude Code or Codex, including the guardrails that make agent output safe to ship: tests, CI gates, review, and scoped permissions.

- A track record integrating GTM systems end to end, such as CRM to billing, CPQ, provisioning, the data warehouse and reverse ETL, pipeline generation workflows.

- Staff-level judgment: you have owned architecture across systems you did not build, made decisions with teams that do not report to you, and changed how a team works.

- Clear writing. Your design docs, PR descriptions and runbooks let others act without a meeting.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- At least 7+ years of Salesforce and full-stack engineering.

- Production experience with Python, TypeScript and Next.js.

- Experience with Chargebee, Stripe, Zuora or another subscription billing platform, including usage-based or marketplace billing (AWS, GCP, GitHub Marketplace).

- Experience building MCP servers, LLM

Datenpflege & Systemarbeit

- Erfahrung mit ERP-Systemen (z. B. Reybex, SAP) und Dispositionstools

Das sind die Charakterzüge, die dich beschreiben:

- Du behältst den Überblick, auch wenn es hektisch wird

- Du bringst starke operative Umsetzungsfähigkeit mit

- Du kommunizierst klar, sachlich und lösungsorientiert

- Du denkst analytisch und triffst auch unter Zeitdruck fundierte Entscheidungen

Das erwartet dich bei uns:

Wir freuen uns auf dich!

Yay! Du hast es bis hierher geschafft!

Wenn du jetzt immer noch liest, ist die Wahrscheinlichkeit groß, dass wir ein Match sind.

Eine Sache liegt uns aber noch auf dem Herzen:
Trau dich! Vor allem als Frau, oder als jemand einer unterrepräsentierten Bevölkerungsgruppe. description:
About the role
As the Principal Enterprise Data Platform Architect, you will serve as the technical lead and pillar head for Data Platform Engineering within the Data Excellence & AI Foundations organization. Reporting directly to the Director of Data Excellence & AI Foundations, you will be responsible for defining, architecting, and evolving Avery Dennison ’s enterprise 10-Layer Data & AI Operating System. In this role, you will lead the technical transition from legacy ETL pipelines toward a modern, high-code Platform Engineering practice grounded in GitOps, Data-as-Code, declarative management, and automated metadata control planes while mentoring and elevating internal engineering talent.
Key Responsibilities
Position Location: Remote

• Own the global architecture blueprint and technology decision trees for Avery Dennison 's enterprise analytical and AI platforms, architecting the 10-Layer Modern Data Operating System across multi-cloud environments (OCI, GCP, Azure).

• Architect and deploy the centralized Metadata Control Plane and automated Data Catalog, coordinating schema tracking, lineage graphs, data quality observability, GitOps methodologies, reusable developer toolboxes, and context-as-code for LLM reasoning.

• Design and govern enterprise AI infrastructure standards, including Vector Databases, Knowledge Graphs, Feature Stores, and RAG pipelines for corporate Gemini LLM solutions and autonomous AI agents with deterministic verification mechanisms.

• Design and enforce the Universal Security Model incorporating Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC), fine-grained masking, and Okta/Active Directory identity integration, while implementing SRE-style observability for platform health, latency, query performance, and compute costs.

• Serve as Pillar Lead for the Data Platform Engineering squad, guiding and mentoring technical talent across pipeline, data, analytics, AI/LLM, DevOps, and APEX engineering while partnering with HR on technical career progression tracks and competency matrices.

Qualifications

• Master’s or Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related quantitative field with 10+ years in enterprise data architecture, platform engineering, or cloud infrastructure design (including 3+ years leading technical teams in a global enterprise context).

• Expert technical proficiency in multi-cloud environments (OCI, GCP, Azure), Oracle ADW (23c/26ai), Databricks, and Apache Iceberg or Delta Lake table formats.

• High-code data engineering mastery in Python, SQL, Apache Airflow, Kafka/Confluent streaming, Change Data Capture (CDC / GoldenGate), Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, and GitOps CI/CD deployment pipelines (GitHub Actions/GitLab CI).

• Direct experience architecting enterprise AI/ML infrastructure, including Vector DBs, Knowledge Graphs, Feature Stores, RAG pipelines, and enterprise LLM integrations (Gemini).

• Strong strategic leadership and communication skills with a proven track record of mentoring technical talent, establishing Universal Security Models (ABAC, RLS, Okta/AD), and presenting complex architectural blueprints to executive sponsors (VP/CIO).

description:
Description du poste
La business unit Digital Customer accompagne les grandes entreprises des secteurs Retail, Luxe, Biens de consommation, Services dans l’accélération de leurs stratégies digitales. Au sein de la BU DC, l'offre Digital Makers (50 Designers, 100 Product Owners/Managers, 50 développeurs et 100 Data Analysts/Scientists au sein de l'offre) accompagne les entreprises dans la réalisation de leurs projets digitaux. Cet accompagnement de bout en bout se base sur plusieurs axes d'action parmi lesquels :

• l'identification précise des problématiques et enjeux à adresser à travers le déroulement rigoureux d'une démarche centrée utilisateurs itérative afin de booster l'adoption

• l'amélioration de l'efficacité et de la scalabilité des méthodes à travers l'automatisation, l'industrialisation, et l'IA

• la passation fluide entre les équipes de conception et les équipes de réalisation permettant d'accélérer la production et d'en améliorer la qualité

L’UX est l’expérience utilisateur, l’émotion, l’intuition et la connexion que l’utilisateur.rice ressent quand il utilise un site ou un produit. La conception de cette expérience utilisateur devient un élément différenciant dans des marchés de plus en plus compétitifs. On parle aujourd’hui d’UX 360° car l’expérience utilisateur est confrontée à des enjeux complexes liés à la diversité des canaux (omnicanalité, parcours phygitaux...), à l'attente d’expériences hyper-personnalisées par les utilisateurs, à la nécessité d'assurer l'accessibilité des produits et leur éco-conception, et à la protection des données, tout en tirant parti des dernières avancées technologiques pour offrir une expérience utilisateur exceptionnelle et en constante évolution.
Dans ce contexte, Wavestone accompagne les Grands Comptes pour les aider à améliorer l'expérience utilisateur de leurs applications tout en favorisant l'industrialisation de l’UX Design au sein de leur DSI.
Objectifs du stage
L’objectif de ce stage sera de développer des connaissances, des convictions et un savoir-faire de premier plan sur un des nombreux sujets que recouvre l’UX Design. Les résultats devront apporter à Wavestone des atouts différenciateurs sur le marché.
Parmi les thématiques prioritaires de la practice, le ou la stagiaire pourra explorer l’impact de l’intelligence artificielle sur les métiers de l’UX. Ces technologies transforment en profondeur la conception, l’évaluation et l’évolution des services numériques, en ouvrant de nouvelles opportunités pour comprendre les utilisateurs, personnaliser les expériences et optimiser les processus de conception. Dans ce contexte, le stage pourra s’articuler autour de plusieurs axes :

• UX et expérience client augmentées par l’IA : analyser l’impact de l’IA sur les comportements utilisateurs, identifier les nouveaux standards d’expérience et définir des recommandations adaptées aux enjeux de nos clients.

• IA et Data au service des designers : explorer les outils et méthodes exploitant l’IA et les données pour accélérer la recherche utilisateur, l’idéation, la conception et l’évaluation des expériences.

• Industrialisation de l’UX grâce à l’IA : étudier comment l’IA, les Design Systems et l’automatisation permettent de concevoir des expériences plus cohérentes, efficaces et scalables.

Le stage mêlera veille, recherche, expérimentation et contribution à des cas d’usage concrets afin d’accompagner les équipes et les clients dans l’adoption de ces nouveaux leviers.
Travaux à réaliser
Le ou la stagiaire viendra faire grandir l’offre interne de Wavestone sur le futur de l’UX et l’UX Design. Sous la supervision d’un.e tuteur.rice de stage, et en s’appuyant sur les éléments de capitalisation déjà en place, le ou la stagiaire aura pour responsabilité de :

• Conduire des entretiens / animer des ateliers avec des consultants de Wavestone pour recueillir leurs retours d’expérience et s’appuyer sur l’expertise cabinet ;

• Recenser les bonnes pratiques du marché actuel et les tendan

title: Supervisor, Child Safety Operations
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

SpaceXSI’s Safety team protects free expression while ensuring our users can safely and successfully engage with our platform through robust policy enforcement. Child Safety is our highest-stakes area: the team identifies, investigates, and removes child sexual exploitation (CSE) and child sexual abuse material (CSAM) across X and Grok products, including AI-generated content, and makes the legally required reports to NCMEC. As we increasingly leverage AI-based automation, we innovate and experiment at a fast pace, striving to be a learning organization with a growth mindset.

As Supervisor, Child Safety, you will lead the Austin-based Child Safety analyst team across shifts. You will be hands-on with escalations, own the quality and defensibility of every high-risk decision, and coordinate with Safety leadership, Legal, and law enforcement response teams on high-profile cases. You will lead the team’s shift from scaled manual review to analysts focused on “Automation First” appeals, model evaluations and audits, investigations, and escalations.

• Own NCMEC reporting decisions for the team. Ensure every report, suspension, and bounce is accurate, well-documented, and meets legal obligations, and that the team knows when to escalate to Legal.

• Coordinate with Safety leadership, Legal, Engineering, and Policy on high-profile cases and action items with Head of Safety visibility. Communicate business needs clearly, close the loop on every action item, and do the due diligence before decisions go up.

• Run the team’s response to viral incidents and emerging abuse trends (e.g., leaked content of minors, AI-altered imagery, election-period trends): organize sweeps, track results, and escalate patterns quickly.

• Take an automation-first approach. Partner with Program Leads to calibrate classifiers and Grok enforcement, track false positives and repeated suspension/unsuspension patterns, and turn findings into concrete improvements.

• Lead the team’s operational model evaluations, audits, and labeling work for CSE, ensuring high-quality curated data that improves Grok’s ability to detect and act on child safety violations.

• Use querying languages (e.g., SQL or Python) and LLM-powered agents to analyze operational data, identify trends, and drive data-informed improvements to policies and processes. Build that habit across the team.

description:
Your Impact at LILA

We're building a talent-dense, high-agency AI safety team at Lila that will engage all core teams within the organization (science, model training, lab integration, etc.), to identify and mitigate risks from scientific superintelligence while retaining the core scientific discovery capabilities of the stack. The initial focus of this team will be to build and implement a bespoke safety strategy for Lila, tailored to its specific goals and deployment strategies. This will involve technical safety strategy development, broader ecosystem engagement, safety-focused evaluations, safety systems to mitigate risks, and a research agenda that explores longer-term needs such as oversight of superintelligent scientific systems.

You will conduct original computational biology research for AI safety and build an integrated understanding of biological risks. You will investigate how capabilities across large language models, specialized biological models, agents and automated laboratories combine to change what is biologically feasible. Our work spans protein and nucleic-acid design, cellular systems and biological delivery; we welcome other specialisms that bring relevant scientific depth and risk judgment.

What You'll Be Building

• Formulate and pursue original computational biology research questions relevant to safety, developing computational approaches and designing and running studies that generate new evidence about biological capabilities, risks and safeguards.

• Combine your research with literature, model assessments, experimental findings and expert input to judge biological feasibility, uncertainty and the significance of emerging capabilities for misuse.

• Identify gaps in expertise, frame questions for external specialists and critically integrate their findings with support from the expert-program team.

• Translate scientific risk judgments into dual-use policy boundaries, evaluation priorities and mitigation requirements that preserve beneficial biological research.

• Work with threat modelers, automated-safety researchers, experimental scientists and mitigation engineers to design informative evaluations and red-teaming studies, test assumptions and assess safeguards.

What You'll Need to Succeed

• Deep expertise (a PhD, or comparable experience) in computational biology or a related quantitative biological discipline, with a record of original research from question formulation and computational study design through to defensible findings.

• Substantive experience assessing biological dual-use risks, with a strong understanding of relevant harmful applications, including pathogen- or toxin-related risks or other consequential biological misuse.

• Prior experience applying biological expertise to AI safety through analysis informing threat models, evaluation or red-teaming work, or mitigation design.

• Sound judgment about the relationship between computational predictions, biological function and experimental evidence, including uncertainty and the limits of your expertise.

• Strong quantitative analysis and scientific programming skills, with the ability to develop computational approaches, run reproducible studies and critically investigate model outputs and biological data.

• The ability to investigate unfamiliar questions, identify appropriate specialists and communicate defensible conclusions across scientific, engineering and policy teams.

• Experience connecting biological modeling or design to experimental validation, including workflows combining LLMs, specialized models, agents or laboratory automation.

title: City Launcher, Groningen
description:
Monumental is automating on-site construction with robotics and software. Our mission is to make construction software-defined and autonomous - a future where beautiful, bespoke buildings go up in a single day, with minimal labour.

We're a growing team of engineers, operators and technicians from companies like Palantir, Qualcomm, Dyson, Shopify, Tesla, Meta and Google DeepMind. It's still the early days of building the company, and this is a chance to make an outsized impact on a problem that matters. From day one, you’ll be working with an experienced founding team, backed by a $32M Series B led by Khosla Ventures and Plural.

Monumental is based in the city centre of Amsterdam, in a beautiful facility with an fully equipped workshop and robot testing floor. We build the whole stack in-house - hardware and software, we're explicitly not a hybrid or remote-first company - you can't build robots or walls from home, so we're onsite five days a week.

 

Read more on why we believe you should spend your time working on construction, and learn about our vision https://www.monumental.co/our-vision/ and company https://www.monumental.co/about/. You might enjoy our YouTube Channel https://www.youtube.com/@buildmonumental, Based in Europe’s film on how we’re fixing Europe’s housing shortage https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2-Q2F0Fcx4A, or this video by Andreas Klinger of what our office looks like https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DOo8n19XEns.

About the role

Over the last few years, Monumental has gone from developing a product that works and delivering our first pilots to building at scale - a fleet of 150+ robots that have laid bricks for 90+ homes, a school, a community centre, a hotel, and 150+ m of canal walls.

We're taking on more construction projects - "deployments" - every month, with more robots, more people, and now in new markets as we scale from the Netherlands into the UK and US.

As Hub Lead, you’ll stand up our first hub outside HQ, in the north of the Netherlands. You’ll start by running our largest deployment to date, then build the team and operations around it as the project pipeline ramps up behind you.

We're hiring versatile operators who want to run a deployment as if it were their own business. Behind every one of these projects is a Deployment Manager who owns it end to end. In practice this is five jobs in one: site foreman, operations manager, account executive, analyst, and project manager. You make the build plan, deploy yourself with your team on site as a subcontractor, manage the contractor relationship, and take responsibility for delivering quality walls, finished on time - in construction, one of the most chaotic industries there is. Your goal will be to run multiple deployments in parallel, overseeing complex and high stakes projects.

One day you're up at dawn, travelling to site, cutting bricks, running the schedule, working with the general contractor and watching your build plan go up brick by brick. The next you'll be at our facility analysing your deployment's P&L and building the systems that improve your margin on the next deployment. You’ll own delivery and translating friction you observe on-site to our R&D team.

This is hard, on-site operations, and some of the most rewarding work you'll find. Robots break, weather turns, the contractor changes the plan, and it's on you to keep the build moving.
You'll have an extraordinary amount of autonomy. It's an excellent fit if you've founded a company before, or if you're looking for an entrepreneurial role where you can make outsized impact.

What you’ll do

- Plan the logistics of a deployment: decide how many and which robots and humans to send, coordinate with other subcontractors, and make both a day-to-day operational plan while also thinking about the bigger picture and how your decisions impact our unit economics.

- Spend time on the construction site, overseeing, managing, and motivating the team; liaising with the general contractor

title: Sr. Manager, Power Plant Operations - Memphis
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

The Sr. Manager of Memphis Power Plant Operations provides strategic and operational leadership for the gas turbine power generation facility supporting SpaceXSI's Colossus data center campus in Memphis, Tennessee. This role oversees all plant operations, maintenance, commissioning, and continued construction/expansion of the dedicated power plant, with full ownership of delivering reliable, high-availability electrical power to the Colossus AI training clusters. The position is responsible for driving operational excellence, ensuring 24/7 power reliability and quality, safety, environmental compliance, and leading cross-functional teams to achieve aggressive scale-up, availability, cost, and schedule objectives in a high-growth, fast-paced environment.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Provide strategic and operational leadership for the Memphis gas turbine power plant, including 24/7 operations, maintenance, commissioning, and ongoing construction and capacity expansion

• Own end-to-end delivery of electrical power to the Colossus data center sites, ensuring industry-leading reliability, availability, power quality, and redundancy

• Lead multidisciplinary teams of operators, maintenance technicians, engineers, contractors, and support staff in a 24/7 operational and construction environment

• Oversee plant performance, commissioning, testing, and seamless integration with data center electrical infrastructure and load

• Develop and execute comprehensive operations and maintenance strategies, including preventative/predictive maintenance, outage planning, hot gas path management, and OEM coordination for gas turbines, generators, balance of plant, and high-voltage electrical systems

• Manage concurrent construction, equipment installation, civil works, and phased capacity expansions while maintaining safe, reliable operation of the existing plant

• Ensure full compliance with environmental, safety, and regulatory requirements, including air permits, emissions controls, TDEC, EPA, OSHA, and local authorities

• Partner closely with SpaceXSI data center operations, engineering, fuel suppliers, OEMs, utilities, and regulatory agencies

• Formulate and execute operating budgets, fuel management, O&M, capital projects, and annual operating plans

• Drive continuous improvement in plant availability, heat rate, emissions, cost, safety metrics, and operational processes

• Establish and promote a culture of uncompromising safety, accountability, operational excellence, rapid execution, and collaboration

• Serve as the site leader and primary representative to the Memphis community, regulators, and stakeholders

• Recruit, develop, coach, and retain high-performing talent; manage staffing, resource allocation, and contractor oversight for both operations and construction

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor’s degree 

• 8+ years of experience in power generation operations, plant management, or related industrial or aerospace operations

• 3+ years of leadership experience managing teams of operators, technicians, and engineers

• Experience operating or managing gas turbine power plants (simple cycle or combined cycle)

Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

The Opportunity:
We’re looking for an enthusiastic, tech-forward product marketer to grow our Observability products by boldly positioning them and running campaigns to attract, convert and retain customers. As a Senior Product Marketing Manager, you will be in charge of the messaging and positioning for a broad product area. Then you’ll work closely with product managers and the marketing team to deliver campaigns, content, events, and training that help buyers buy (and sellers sell) our value.
Product Marketing lives within the Product org rather than the Marketing org at Grafana Labs , and we think differently about the job. Rather than purely executing launches or campaigns, we want PMMs to teach product managers and engineers in our org how to think about growth and demand, and to codify product marketing knowledge into AI-forward tools and processes that anyone in the organization can use. For example, we all contribute product information to a shared knowledge base, which we use to generate enablement materials and decks.
Grafana Labs is a fast-paced and growing organization. As such, this role requires strategic skills, an interest in teaching, and hands-on tactical execution (blogs, webinar outlines, video scripts, etc). Our team is full of people who crave impact and independence - if you are seeking a role with narrow scope where you run a defined playbook, this is not the job for you.
What You'll Be Doing:

• Actively partner with and teach product managers to define product value, messaging, and go-to-market strategy, from competitive positioning to sales enablement collateral.

• Partner with product management, engineering and various go-to-market functions to create materials that help customers evaluate and adopt our products: reference architectures, implementation guides, detailed product information and more.

• Own customer lifecycle campaigns (competitive positioning, retention, upsell/cross-sell) to strategically shape marketing programs and drive growth across the entire customer journey.

• Conduct market and customer research to understand pain points, competition and opportunities.

• Teach go-to-market and sales teams our products’ capabilities and the value they provide, deliver training and enablement, ensure customer facing teams are able to effectively engage with customers, partners, and prospects.

What Makes You a Great Fit:

• 4+ years of relevant experience (product marketing, solutions marketing, product management)

• Experience with marketing and selling to a technical audience

• A passion for open source, cloud native, and infrastructure technologies

OpenAI's Global Network Infrastructure team is responsible for building and operating the global network backbone that connects our rapidly expanding compute infrastructure. Our work enables reliable, high-performance connectivity across data centers, cloud service providers, and network points of presence (PoPs), supporting the infrastructure behind OpenAI's research and products.

As OpenAI continues to scale its compute footprint globally, we are expanding our network infrastructure to meet increasing demands for capacity, reliability, and operational efficiency. Our team works across physical network design, carrier connectivity, network deployment, and operational troubleshooting to deliver resilient infrastructure at exceptional scale.

We are looking for a hands-on Network Infrastructure Engineer to help design, deploy, activate, and operate OpenAI's global wide area network (WAN) infrastructure.

In this role, you will take direct ownership of bringing new network connectivity online, working closely with fiber providers, cloud service providers, and internal infrastructure teams to establish reliable connectivity across our global backbone.

title: Program Manager, Local Community Impact
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Our Community team builds direct relationships with people who use OpenAI’s technology, helps others learn from their experiences, and brings their insights back to product and research teams. Our programs connect communities with trusted partners who help organizations adopt AI effectively.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re hiring a Program Manager to build and run our partner network. You will turn an early program into a reliable operation: recruit and onboard partners, coordinate agreements and payments, manage external service providers, support local events and marketing, review service quality, and improve the program as we learn.

This partner network will be on the ground in communities helping people-from small businesses, non-profits, and community organizations-experience concrete benefits from our technology. They will set up useful workflows, learn OpenAI tools and become more confident, independent users.

You should be as comfortable helping a partner resolve an onboarding issue as you are designing the systems that prevent it from happening again. You will work with local operators and internal teams to make sure commitments are clear, work gets done, and the people we serve receive useful, high-quality support.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

- Build the partner operating model, from sourcing and selection of partners through onboarding, ongoing support, renewal and exit. Establish clear expectations, owners, timelines and escalation paths. Create a scalable operating model that supports program growth and evolving partner needs.

- Run partner onboarding with Legal, Finance and Procurement: track agreements, required information, vendor setup, readiness and start dates so partners can begin work and receive payments through approved processes.

- Manage partner payments, reporting and related operational processes.

- Plan and support local workshops, deployments and events with partners. Coordinate audiences, venues, budgets, materials, staffing and follow-up while preserving local ownership.

- Coordinate program marketing and communications with Community, Marketing and content partners. Develop clear partner guidance, route brand and messaging approvals, and help useful stories and practices reach the right audiences.

- Build trusted relationships with local operators and the organizations they serve. Coach partners, answer questions, address service-quality concerns and set clear boundaries around access, funding and program participation.

- Create practical systems for the partner community: intake, a shared knowledge base, service logs, regular check-ins and reusable playbooks that reduce manual work without sacrificing quality.

- Develop and operate partner review processes with the hiring manager and relevant teams. Combine verified service delivery, beneficiary feedback and sustained product use to understand performance and improve support.

- Collaborate with analytics and product teams to assess program impact using appropriate data and feedback.

- Manage budgets, vendors, risks and dependencies across the program. Keep stakeholders informed, surface decisions early and bring recurring partner feedback into program and product improvements.

YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU

- 8+ years owning a complex partner, community or operational program from early design through execution at scale, with clear examples of what you personally built and improved.

- Bring strong operational judgment and follow-through across onboarding, financial workflows, events and multiple stakeholder groups.

- Can earn trust with small-business owners, local technical operators and community leaders, explain expectations plainly and have difficult conversations when needed.

- Have practical familiarity with ChatGPT, Codex and AI-enabled workflows, and can work credibly with technical specialists while explaining tools to people with less technical experience.

- Use data and qualitative feedback to distinguish meaning

The insurance industry is a $1T market that’s remained largely untouched by the digital revolution, and PolicyMe is here to change that. • Defining the strategy and roadmap to make us the go-to provider for all of our customers’ personal insurance needs, including the platform-wide programs and features that drive multi-product adoption

• Building trust digitally across the products we offer, so customers feel similar levels of confidence and reassurance as they would get when they speak with one our licensed advisors

title: CRM Solutions Lead
description:
Our product runs on our clients' data, and that data lives in their CRM. This role owns it end to end.
You'll work directly with clients to understand what's in their CRM - Salesforce, HubSpot, GoHighLevel, Zoho or whatever else they run on - diagnose the data quality problems, define how it maps into our warehouse, and turn it into segments our campaign teams can act on. Once a client is live, you own the ongoing execution: loads, extracts, dedupes and segment builds.
Internally, you'll work closely with our data engineering and data science teams, giving them the inputs they need to build and run ingestion from each client CRM into our warehouse.
This role needs both kinds of strength. You need the technical depth to profile CRM data at scale and safely load it into a production instance, and the client-facing judgment to turn what you find into recommendations a client will act on.
Responsibilities
• Run discovery sessions with a client's sales, marketing and technical teams to understand how their CRM is actually used, and serve as our technical lead in the client relationship
• Document CRM structure: object models, custom objects and fields, picklists, record types, relationships, automations and integrations
• Profile CRM records across standard and custom objects for completeness, duplication, staleness, formatting inconsistency, invalid values and broken relationships, and quantify what you find
• Recommend how to address what you find, and take those recommendations to the client: what they need to fix at source, what we can resolve on our side, and what to exclude
• Translate available data into segments that are both technically buildable and commercially meaningful, in partnership with our campaign teams
• Build source-to-target field mappings into our data warehouse, specifying transformation logic, data types, picklist normalization, null handling, identity resolution keys and sync cadence
• Partner with data engineering and data science on the ingestion build, supplying the field definitions, business logic, sample data and validation rules they need, and stay engaged through build, testing and reconciliation
• Load records into client CRMs and extract them back out at volume, using native tools, data loaders and REST/Bulk APIs, owning staging, dry runs, dedupe rules and rollback plans
Requirements
• 5+ years in RevOps, marketing ops, GTM engineering, solutions consulting, sales engineering or CRM consulting, with real operational ownership
• Direct experience owning client relationships and leading client-facing engagements
• Ability to run a discovery session with a skeptical stakeholder and leave with better information than you came in with
• Comfortable presenting evaluation findings and recommendations to client stakeholders, including when those findings are critical of their existing data or processes
• At leasts 3 years of deep, hands-on experience with at least two major CRMs (Salesforce and HubSpot preferred): object models, admin configuration, import/export tooling, REST and Bulk APIs
• Proven bulk data operations at volume: loads, upserts, merges, dedupes and write-backs into production systems, with the judgment to do them safely
• Data quality experience: profiling, deduplication, standardization, enrichment, identity resolution
• SQL proficiency and strong spreadsheet skills
• Experience producing source-to-target mapping documentation for an engineering audience
• Clear written communication
Preferred requirements
• Working knowledge of GoHighLevel, Zoho, Dynamics, Pipedrive or Close
• Python or similar for profiling, transformation scripts and API-driven bulk operations
• Familiarity with warehouse and ELT stacks - we use Databricks, dbt and Fivetran, though experience with Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift or Airbyte translates well
• Experience in commercial real estate or real estate: CRM, data or operations work in the industry
• Comfortable using AI tools to move faster on the work - profili

title: QA I Coding Operations

The QA I, is an integral member of the Risk Adjustment Coding Team. The QA position monitors & reports on the accuracy of all coding performed by Cotiviti coders and/or third party partner coders. This position provides direct coaching and feedback to coders. The QA I conducts QA and audit reviews, supports remediation for risk adjustment coding services, and ensures compliance with quality standards.
Responsibilities

• Provides Quality Assurance feedback by working as a liaison between Coder I, Coder II and the Team Lead to ensure coding is complete and accurate. Reviews a defined percentage of the Coder I and Coder II work to ensure quality standards are met and maintained.

• Completes chart or encounter review for proper HCC-mapped diagnosis coding from various chart types (physician, facility, non-facility).

• Completes chart or encounter review for proper HCC-mapped diagnosis coding performedprospectively, concurrent, or retrospective.

• Ensures that all coding performed follows client specific or industry standard coding guidelinesand reflects an accurate and complete representation of the documentation within the medicalrecord.

• Professionally communicates findings, errors, and any suggestions to all staff to facilitate ongoing communications and efficient department operations.

Professionally communicates finds, errors, and any suggestions to all staff in order to facilitate on-going communications and efficient department operations.

• Completes internal audits as necessary to support quality accuracy.

• Responds to questions via the ‘Questions Queue’ for individual coders.

• Reviews internal system reports on quality of work for all assigned Clinical Coder Specialists. These reports are reviewed daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly and yearly as needed.

• Communicate quality issues and trends to the Team lead, Coding Manager and Training Manager.

• Recommend additional training based on results of the quality audit for those Coder I and Coder II where they fall behind the 95% accuracy rate.

• Develop an action plan in collaboration with the Team Lead and Manager as needed with regard to improvement in the quality of work for a Coder I or II and reports progress to the Team Lead.

• Utilize Cotiviti training tools and coding library for questions.
